questions.question: What is a unit cell in crystallography?

answers.a: The smallest repeating unit that can build up the entire crystal lattice through translation.
answers.b: A single atom within a crystal.
answers.c: A defect in the crystal structure.
answers.d: The outermost layer of a crystal.

explanations.a: A unit cell is the smallest repeating unit in a crystal lattice that, through translational repetition, can recreate the entire structure.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a primitive unit cell?

answers.a: Contains more than one lattice point.
answers.c: Has atoms only at the center.

explanations.b: A primitive unit cell contains only one lattice point, typically with atoms located at the vertices.

questions.question: How many types of Bravais lattices are there in three-dimensional space?

explanations.b: There are 14 distinct Bravais lattices in three-dimensional space, corresponding to the seven crystal systems.

questions.question: In a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice, how many atoms are effectively contained within one unit cell?

explanations.c: An FCC unit cell has atoms at each corner (1/8 contribution each) and at the center of each face (1/2 contribution each), totaling 4 atoms.

questions.question: Which of the following crystal systems has all sides equal and all angles equal to 90 degrees?

explanations.c: In the cubic crystal system, all sides are equal in length, and all angles are 90 degrees.

questions.question: What distinguishes a non-primitive unit cell from a primitive one?

answers.a: Non-primitive unit cells have additional lattice points within the cell, not just at the vertices.
answers.b: Non-primitive unit cells are smaller than primitive unit cells.
answers.c: Non-primitive unit cells lack translational symmetry.
answers.d: Non-primitive unit cells are always hexagonal.

explanations.a: Non-primitive unit cells contain additional lattice points, such as at face centers or body centers, beyond those at the vertices.
